outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no source read settles the conjecture in the general form the Wikipedia bullet states; the in-window events are partial (a 2024 revision and 2025–2026 preprints for special classes, a conditional reduction, a metric multiplicity-two case, and a Zariski-equisingularity characterisation that does not touch the topological implication), while the isolated μ-constant family theorem of de Bobadilla and Pełka, first posted to arXiv on 14 April 2022, appeared in Annals of Mathematics in 2024 (accepted 4 March 2024, published online 3 July 2024).
problem_asks: The bullet asks whether topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity of varieties at singular points. Parts: (a) PAIR FORM: if two varieties (complex hypersurface germs in the classical literature; the Wikipedia wording says only 'varieties') at singular points are topologically equivalent, their multiplicities at those points are equal. (b) FAMILY FORM: if a family of varieties is topologically equisingular along a stratum (the singular points varying in a family), the multiplicity is constant along that family, i.e. the family is equimultiple. (c) SCOPE the statement itself leaves open: all dimensions, isolated and non-isolated singularities, complex or real/analytic/algebraic germs, and whether 'varieties' means hypersurfaces. The bullet names no restriction; the literature standardly restricts to complex hypersurface germs. The bullet's links go to 'Algebraic variety' and 'Singular point of an algebraic variety'; the name 'Zariski multiplicity conjecture' is not linked. I record both the pair form and the family form because the sources treat them differently.

events.what_happened: Zariski (with Burau) proved the conjecture for plane curves, n = 2: topologically equivalent plane curve germs have equal multiplicity. Cited as 1932 in search snippets and as 'n = 2 (Zariski)' in the 2024 Silva paper (v2, opened). I did not open the 1932 paper itself.
events.delivers: Plane curve germs only (dimension of the variety one): topological equivalence implies equal multiplicity.
events.remains: Every hypersurface of dimension two or more, all families, non-isolated and metric variants of the general statement.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in the plane-curve case.

events.what_happened: A'Campo and Lê (1973) gave the case of multiplicity one, m(X,0) = 1, as cited in the 2024 Silva paper (v2, opened). Year taken from search snippets; the 1973 paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: Hypersurfaces of multiplicity one: if one of two topologically equivalent germs has multiplicity one, the other does too.
events.remains: Multiplicity two and higher, all families, the general statement.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in the multiplicity-one case.

events.what_happened: Navarro Aznar (1980) handled the case n = 3 with multiplicity two, in the convention of the 2024 Silva paper (v2, opened), which cites it. Year taken from a search snippet; the paper was not opened.
events.delivers: The n = 3 convention of the cited paper with multiplicity two; other multiplicities and dimensions not covered.
events.remains: Other multiplicities, other dimensions, families, the general statement.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in the stated case.

events.what_happened: Ephraim and Trotman showed that multiplicity is preserved under C¹ homeomorphisms (C¹ equivalence), per the Wikipedia-style summaries in search snippets. Not opened; no year established.
events.delivers: If the equivalence is a C¹ homeomorphism, the multiplicities agree.
events.remains: Topological (merely continuous) equivalence, which is the conjecture's hypothesis.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture under a stronger regularity hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Greuel and O'Shea: families where the leading function f0 is weighted homogeneous and the Milnor number is constant are equimultiple (per search snippets citing them). Not opened; year not established.
events.delivers: Isolated hypersurface families whose leading term is weighted homogeneous with constant Milnor number.
events.remains: Non-weighted-homogeneous leading terms, non-isolated singularities, pair form.
events.direction: Supports the family form in a special class.

events.what_happened: Teymuri Garakani (2014): a conditional topological result, that the algebraic multiplicities of two topologically equisingular isolated complex hypersurface germs agree provided the defining topological maps are Lipschitz on a generic real segment through the origin (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: Conditional on Lipschitz regularity of the topological equivalence along a generic real segment.
events.remains: The unconditional statement.
events.doubts: The result is explicitly conditional on a Lipschitz hypothesis that the general conjecture does not contain.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture under an extra Lipschitz hypothesis.

events.what_happened: Plénat and Trotman (arXiv 1202.5177, 2012 by ID): equimultiplicity for μ-constant families of the form f + t g + t² h under a condition on the tangent cone (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: μ-constant families of the stated special form under a tangent-cone condition.
events.remains: General μ-constant families; the topological hypothesis of the conjecture.
events.direction: Supports the family form in a special class.

events.what_happened: Eyral (arXiv 1506.07996, 2015 by ID): for a family of line singularities with homogeneous f0 and constant Lê numbers, the family is equimultiple; applied to topologically V-equisingular families of non-isolated line singularities (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: Non-isolated line singularities with homogeneous f0 and constant Lê numbers; topologically V-equisingular families in that class.
events.remains: Non-homogeneous f0 and general non-isolated singularities.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for non-isolated line singularities in a special class.

events.what_happened: Fernandes and Sampaio (arXiv 1508.06250, 2015 by ID): the multiplicity of complex analytic surfaces in C³ is a bi-Lipschitz invariant (search snippets; not opened). A metric version, not the topological statement.
events.delivers: Metric (bi-Lipschitz) invariance of multiplicity for surfaces in C³, not topological invariance.
events.remains: Topological invariance; metric version in other dimensions.
events.direction: Supports the metric analogue for surfaces; does not decide the topological statement.

events.what_happened: Eyral and Ruas (arXiv 1602.05732, 2016; published International Journal of Mathematics 2019): for line singularities that are weighted homogeneous or Newton non-degenerate, constancy of the first Lê number and polar number gives equimultiplicity (search snippets; not opened).
events.revisions: arXiv 2016, revised 2019; published International Journal of Mathematics 2019 (per search snippet).
events.delivers: Line singularities of the weighted homogeneous or Newton non-degenerate kind under constant first Lê and polar numbers.
events.remains: Other non-isolated singularities; the general statement.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for a class of line singularities.

events.what_happened: Sampaio (arXiv 1709.03373, 2017 by ID): a metric version at infinity for complex algebraic affine sets; the degree is a bi-Lipschitz invariant at infinity when the homeomorphism's Lipschitz constants are close to 1 (search snippets; not opened).
events.delivers: Degree (not multiplicity at a point) is a bi-Lipschitz invariant at infinity under near-1 constants.
events.remains: Multiplicity at singular points and the topological statement.
events.direction: Metric analogue at infinity; does not decide the topological statement.

events.what_happened: O. N. Silva (single author, arXiv 1902.05139, 2019 by ID): a positive answer to the conjecture for a special class of non-isolated singularities in families of map germs C² to C³ (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: A special class of non-isolated map-germ families (C² to C³), per the search snippet.
events.remains: General classes; the 2023 and 2025 Silva papers extend the same theme.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for a special class.

events.what_happened: Brzostowski, Krasiński and Oleksik gave an elementary proof of the conjecture for μ-constant families of non-degenerate singularities, in the Łódź University Press volume Analytic and Algebraic Geometry 4 (2019) (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: μ-constant families of non-degenerate singularities.
events.remains: Degenerate families, non-isolated singularities, the pair form.
events.direction: Supports the family form in a special class.

events.what_happened: Ruas: a positive answer to the conjecture for families of singular surfaces in C³ whose family has a smooth normalisation (search snippet citing Ruas; not opened). Year not established.
events.delivers: Families of surfaces in C³ with smooth normalisation.
events.remains: Surfaces without smooth normalisation; other dimensions.
events.direction: Supports the family form for a special class of surfaces.

events.what_happened: Fernández de Bobadilla and Pełka posted 'Symplectic monodromy at radius zero and equimultiplicity of μ-constant families' to arXiv as 2204.07007 (v1 14 April 2022; opened). The abstract: every family of isolated hypersurface singularities with constant Milnor number has constant multiplicity. Main Theorem 1.1 (ar5iv rendering, opened): for a continuous family of power series f_t with μ(f_t) finite and independent of t, the multiplicity ν(f_t) is independent of t. Method: the A'Campo model of radius-zero monodromy is given a symplectic structure, and a generalised McLean spectral sequence for fixed-point Floer homology is used. Published in Annals of Mathematics 200(1), 2024, pp. 153–299, DOI 10.4007/annals.2024.200.1.4 (publication dates from the Annals page, opened).
events.revisions: v1 14 Apr 2022; v2 28 Jun 2022; v3 8 Sep 2022; v4 26 Dec 2022; v5 5 Mar 2024 (inside the window; I did not check what v5 changed). Journal: received 28 Jun 2022, revised 22 Feb 2024, accepted 4 Mar 2024, published online 3 Jul 2024 (Annals page).
events.delivers: Establishes the family form for isolated hypersurface singularities: a family with constant (finite) Milnor number has constant multiplicity. Restricted to (i) isolated singularities, (ii) hypersurface germs given by power series, (iii) families along which the Milnor number is constant (μ-constancy is the hypothesis, not stated topological equisingularity), with the link to topological equisingularity running through Lê–Ramanujam, which the sources say covers the case when the number of variables is not 3.
events.remains: (1) Non-isolated singularities (not covered; Massey 2022 gives a non-isolated version only for aligned hypersurfaces). (2) Families that are topologically equisingular but with non-constant Milnor number, if any, for the case where Lê–Ramanujam does not apply (number of variables 3). (3) The single-pair form (two topologically equivalent isolated germs, no family), which Sampaio (2025) says is still open; see disputes. (4) Varieties other than hypersurface germs. (5) The metric and bi-Lipschitz versions.

checked_by.qualification: The journal of record for research mathematics; referees are chosen by the editors.
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted the article on 4 March 2024 after revision (received 28 June 2022, revised 22 February 2024), per the Annals page.

checked_by.who: Shamuel Auyeung (Stony Brook PhD, advisor Mark McLean)
checked_by.qualification: Doctoral researcher working in fixed-point Floer theory, the toolkit this proof uses.
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a second, independent proof of the isolated family case using the TQFT structure of fixed-point Floer cohomology (arXiv 2308.13925, Aug 2023). This is a re-derivation, not a referee check of the original.

checked_by.qualification: Singularity theorist; named in Sampaio's abstract as one of the authors of the 2022 Budur–Fernández de Bobadilla–Lê–Nguyen conjecture.
checked_by.what_they_did: Scheduled a 2026 Tsinghua lecture course that presents the proof of the isolated equisingular-family case. This is teaching, not a public verification of the argument.

events.time_since_posted: about 4 years 6 months from arXiv v1 to 13 Oct 2026; about 2 years 7 months from acceptance

machine_checked.system: Lean 4 (ImperialCollegeLondon AnnalsChallenge statement, lean-eval problem annals_symplectic_monodromy)

events.doubts: (1) A 2019 Łódź-press paper (search snippet; not opened) says the 80-page manuscript was not yet published in a recognised journal and needs independent confirmation. That predates the Annals acceptance and is not a current objection. (2) Sampaio (arXiv 2503.17127, 2025) says the Zariski conjecture 'is still an open problem even in the case of germ of complex analytic functions with isolated singularities'. That disagrees with the reading of Auyeung and Budur about the pair form. It is a scope disagreement, not an identified error in the proof. (3) No zbMATH or MathSciNet review was reachable, so I cannot say how reviewers described the scope. (4) The Lean formalisation of the statement is not a complete proof: its page shows 'declaration uses sorry'.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: proves that a constant Milnor number in an isolated family forces constant multiplicity, so the family form holds in this class. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Massey (arXiv 2209.03939, 23 Aug 2022): 'We show that the Theorem of Bobadilla and Pełka implies a non-isolated version for aligned hyper surface singularities' (abstract, opened). Derived from the Bobadilla–Pełka theorem; the full text was not read.
events.revisions: v1 23 Aug 2022 (only version seen on the abstract page).
events.delivers: Non-isolated singularities of the 'aligned' kind (the abstract does not define it; the full text was not read): the Bobadilla–Pełka consequence.
events.remains: Non-aligned non-isolated singularities; pair form.
events.doubts: The class ('aligned') is not defined in the abstract, and the full text was not read, so the exact scope is not established.
events.direction: Supports the family form for a non-isolated class.

events.what_happened: Auyeung (sole author), 'Adjacent Singularities, TQFTs, and Zariski's Multiplicity Conjecture', arXiv 2308.13925 (v1 26 Aug 2023; 34 pages, 10 figures; opened). The abstract calls it a new proof of Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for isolated hypersurface singularities, first proved by de Bobadilla and Pełka. Theorem 1.3 (ar5iv, opened): a family of isolated hypersurface singularities whose members are adjacent all have the same Milnor number μ; then each member has the same multiplicity and the same log canonical threshold. Method: TQFT structure of fixed-point Floer cohomology, symplectic cobordisms between Milnor fibrations of adjacent singularities, and a McLean spectral sequence. It recovers a theorem of Varchenko. Author's Stony Brook dissertation (2023) contains the same material (search snippet).
events.revisions: v1 26 Aug 2023; the abstract page shows no later version and no journal reference or journal DOI.
events.delivers: Re-proves the family form for isolated hypersurfaces under an adjacency hypothesis: adjacent members with constant Milnor number have constant multiplicity and constant log canonical threshold. The single-pair topological form is not what Theorem 1.3 states.
events.remains: Non-isolated singularities; families without adjacency; the single-pair form; the general statement.
events.doubts: Arxiv-only; no journal reference found on the abstract page. A talk was given at UNM (27 March 2024, search snippet) but no review. The abstract's phrase 'Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for isolated hypersurface singularities' is wider than Theorem 1.3, which needs adjacency and constant Milnor number. Both readings are recorded here; the later pass decides.
events.direction: Supports the family form for isolated hypersurfaces in an adjacency class.

events.what_happened: O. N. Silva posted 'On Zariski multiplicity conjecture for quasihomogeneous surfaces with non-isolated singularities' as arXiv 2309.02624 (v1 6 Sep 2023; v1 text not opened). The v2 of 20 Jul 2024 (opened) is the same surface result: Theorem 1.1 covers irreducible surfaces in (C³,0) that are zero sets of reduced quasihomogeneous germs, with smooth normalisation and only transverse double points away from the origin. If two such surfaces are topologically equivalent, m(X,0) = m(Y,0). v2 states 'Conjecture 1 above is still open'. The date is taken from v1 on the basis that the surface theorem is its content; the v1 text was not read to confirm this.
events.revisions: v1 6 Sep 2023 (text not opened); v2 20 Jul 2024 (inside the window; same surface theorem; retitled 'On Zariski multiplicity conjecture for quasihomogeneous surfaces with non-isolated singularities'; still states the general conjecture open); v3 8 Nov 2025 (inside the window; new title; adds the n-dimensional Theorem 1.2, see its own event).
events.delivers: Surfaces in C³ with non-isolated singularities of the stated type (quasihomogeneous, smooth normalisation, transverse double points off the origin): topological equivalence implies equal multiplicity at 0.
events.remains: Hypersurfaces of other dimensions in v3 (see its own event); non-quasihomogeneous germs; families; the general conjecture.
events.doubts: Only arXiv versions found; no journal publication or referee report located. The authors' own v2 (inside the window) says Conjecture 1 is still open and proves only special cases, so the claim is about a class, not the general problem.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for the stated surface class.

events.what_happened: Sampaio, 'On the Milnor fibres of initial forms of topologically equivalent holomorphic functions', arXiv 2503.17127 (21 Mar 2025; opened). Affirms, for plane curves, the Budur–Fernández de Bobadilla–Lê–Nguyen conjecture that topologically equivalent germs have initial forms with homotopy-equivalent Milnor fibres (Prop 2.1). States that a positive answer to that conjecture implies a positive answer to Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for right equivalence and for hypersurfaces with isolated singularities (Props 2.3, 2.4, conditional). The introduction says the Zariski conjecture 'is still an open problem even in the case of germ of complex analytic functions with isolated singularities'.
events.delivers: Plane curves only, for the Milnor-fibre homotopy statement. For Zariski it is a conditional reduction: nothing unconditional for Zariski, and plane-curve Zariski was already known (n = 2).
events.remains: The Zariski conjecture for right equivalence and for isolated hypersurfaces is open unless the Milnor-fibre conjecture holds in higher dimensions; the general conjecture is open.
events.doubts: The Zariski content is conditional and the paper does not claim it settles any case. It cites the Bobadilla–Pełka family result as 'confirmed' for families with isolated singularities, which is the reading in dispute.
events.direction: No cut on the Zariski conjecture itself; a conditional reduction.

events.what_happened: Nogueira da Silva and Silva Júnior, 'Transverse slices, Ruas' conjecture, and Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for quasihomogeneous surfaces', arXiv 2509.01634 (v1 1 Sep 2025; v2 13 Oct 2025; opened, read in full except the first part of the introduction). For finitely determined quasihomogeneous corank-1 map germs (C²,0) to (C³,0): introduces the μ_{m,k}-minimal transverse slice; under that slice hypothesis proves topological triviality equivalent to Whitney equisingularity (Ruas's conjecture in this setting); gives a counterexample to Whitney equisingularity implying bi-Lipschitz equisingularity; and proves (Theorem 5.2) that every topologically trivial 1-parameter unfolding is equimultiple, i.e. Zariski's conjecture for 1-parameter families of these germs. Remark 5.3 leaves the higher-dimensional and higher-corank analogues open. The authors write: 'Zariski's multiplicity conjecture remains open in its original formulation.'
events.revisions: v1 1 Sep 2025; v2 13 Oct 2025 (retitled 'Transverse slices, Ruas' conjecture, and Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for quasihomogeneous surfaces'; the search snippet of v1 was not opened).
events.delivers: Equimultiplicity for 1-parameter families that are topologically trivial, of quasihomogeneous, finitely determined, corank-1 map germs (C²,0) to (C³,0). Note the hypothesis is topological triviality, which is stronger than the equisingularity in the bullet. The slice hypothesis enters the Ruas-equivalence part; whether Theorem 5.2 itself needs it was not confirmed from the text read.
events.remains: Multi-parameter families, higher dimension and higher corank (Remark 5.3), non-quasihomogeneous germs, topologically equisingular families that are not trivial, the single-pair form, and the general conjecture.
events.doubts: (1) Arxiv-only, no referee or expert check found. (2) Same author pair as the 2023–2025 Silva papers, so not an independent team. (3) Hypotheses are narrow: quasihomogeneous, corank 1, 1-parameter, topologically trivial, and the slice hypothesis in the Ruas part.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for one-parameter families in a narrow class of map germs.

events.what_happened: Fernandes, Jelonek and Sampaio, arXiv 2509.03447. v1 (3 Sep 2025; title 'Metric version of the Zariski Multiplicity Conjecture is true for multiplicity two', per the v1 HTML, opened). v2 (17 Dec 2025, retitled 'Proof of the metric Arnold's corank problem'; opened abstract and HTML). Main result: if two germs of analytic hypersurfaces are ambient bi-Lipschitz equivalent and one has multiplicity 2 at 0, so does the other (the multiplicity-two case of the metric Conjecture A, stated in the v1 introduction as 'we show that Conjecture A is true for multiplicity two'). Theorem 3.1 in v2 is the corank statement, not the multiplicity one. v2 abstract also claims a complete positive answer to the metric Arnold corank problem and the three-variable case. The v2 abstract does not mention Zariski. The introduction calls the general metric conjecture 'still open'.
events.revisions: v1 3 Sep 2025 (title: Metric version ... multiplicity two); v2 17 Dec 2025 (title: Proof of the metric Arnold's corank problem; abstract covers the corank problem).
events.delivers: The metric (ambient bi-Lipschitz) version for analytic hypersurfaces, only in the multiplicity-two case. This is an analogue of the bullet: bi-Lipschitz equivalence replaces topological equivalence, so it does not settle the topological statement.
events.remains: The metric conjecture for multiplicity three and above; the topological statement of the bullet in full.
events.doubts: Analogue, not the topological statement; the headline has moved from the Zariski conjecture (v1) to Arnold's corank problem (v2). No referee or expert engagement found.
events.direction: Positive for the metric multiplicity-two case; says nothing decisive about the topological statement.

events.what_happened: Nogueira da Silva and Silva Júnior, arXiv 2309.02624 v3 (8 Nov 2025; opened in two chunks). Retitled 'Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for quasihomogeneous hypersurfaces with non-isolated singularities'. Theorem 1.1 is the surface case (as in v2). Theorem 1.2 (new in v3): for 3 ≤ n ≤ 4, finitely determined, quasihomogeneous, corank-1 map germs f, g: (Cⁿ,0) to (Cⁿ⁺¹,0) with topologically equivalent images, and smooth multiple point spaces D^{n-1}(f) and D^{n-1}(g), the images have equal multiplicity at 0. The abstract says the class is 2 ≤ n ≤ 4. The text says 'More than 50 years later, Zariski's multiplicity conjecture above is still open.' No version comments on the page.
events.revisions: v1 6 Sep 2023 (surfaces; see the 2023 event); v2 20 Jul 2024 (surfaces only, inside the window); v3 8 Nov 2025 (adds Theorem 1.2 and the n = 3, 4 class; this is the first version carrying it, so the date is taken from v3).
events.delivers: Equal multiplicity under topological equivalence for quasihomogeneous, finitely determined, corank-1 map germs with smooth multiple point spaces, in dimensions 3 and 4 (dimension 2 by Theorem 1.1 of the earlier version). Restricted to that class.
events.remains: Germs that are not quasihomogeneous, higher corank, non-smooth multiple point spaces, dimension five and above, families, isolated singularities as a separate case, and the general conjecture (the text calls it still open).
events.doubts: (1) Scope grew between versions: v2 (July 2024) covers surfaces only, and v3 (November 2025) adds dimensions 3 and 4 under the same arXiv identifier with a new title. The abstract says 2 ≤ n ≤ 4 while Theorem 1.2 states 3 ≤ n ≤ 4. (2) The hypotheses are narrow (quasihomogeneous, corank 1, smooth multiple point spaces). (3) No referee report, journal publication or expert check located.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for the stated class.

events.what_happened: Parusiński and Păunescu, 'Zariski equisingularity of surface singularities in C³ by a local invariant', arXiv 2602.15192 (16 Feb 2026; opened). Assigns to each analytic surface singularity in C³ (isolated or not) an invariant mult*(V), built from the multiplicities of successive discriminants under generic corank-one projections. Theorem 0.2: for an analytic family of such surfaces the following are equivalent: ν-transverse Zariski equisingularity after a generic linear change; Zariski equisingularity after a generic change; constancy of mult*. Remark 1.2 notes that Zariski equisingularity implies equimultiplicity. The paper does not mention the Zariski multiplicity conjecture or topological equisingularity.
events.delivers: A characterisation of generic Zariski equisingularity for analytic families of surface singularities in C³ by constancy of mult*. It does not prove that topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity. Its only contact with the bullet is Remark 1.2, which runs the other way (Zariski equisingularity implies equimultiplicity).
events.remains: The whole bullet: topological equisingularity implying equimultiplicity, in any dimension.
events.doubts: Preprint of about 10 pages, not peer-reviewed; no public engagement found.
events.direction: Neither for nor against the conjecture; a neighbouring result on Zariski equisingularity.

events.what_happened: ImperialCollegeLondon 'AnnalsChallenge' repository (v1.0.0 per the lean-eval page; opened on GitHub) and its lean-eval problem 'annals_symplectic_monodromy': a Lean 4 statement of the equimultiplicity theorem of de Bobadilla and Pełka (the lean-eval file AnnalsOfMathematics/2024-200-1-SymplecticMonodromy.lean is named on the page; the file itself was not opened). Per the search snippet of the lean-eval page, the statement concerns a continuous family of multivariable power series on the unit interval with zero constant terms and constant Milnor number, concluding that the order is constant. The repository README says the proofs are not formalised and are left as sorry. The lean-eval page (opened) shows 'All goals completed' next to a warning that the declaration uses sorry. No human and no AI system is credited for the statement or the proof on the pages read. The repository is funded by the Renaissance Philanthropy AI for Math Fund. No date for the statement was found.
events.revisions: Repository version v1.0.0 (commit e32eb14 per the lean-eval page); date not found.
events.delivers: A formal statement of the equimultiplicity conclusion for μ-constant families of power series, i.e. the family form in the isolated case. It is a formalisation of an argument already proved by humans, not an independent proof.
events.remains: The whole formal proof (declaration uses sorry); the non-family, non-isolated and general forms are not formalised here.
events.doubts: Statement-only; the proof is sorry. The lean-eval page shows 'All goals completed' alongside the sorry warning, which is contradictory on its face; the sorry warning is the one to rely on.
events.direction: Formalises the family-form claim of the Bobadilla–Pełka theorem; no cut of its own.

events.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts, each claiming a negative answer to Zariski's question whether embedded topology determines multiplicity for complex hypersurface germs. (1) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three' (dated 24 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there is a finite N > 3 divisible by eight (the text gives N = 4s₀ + 16, where s₀ is the variable count of two seed polynomials fixed by an integer relation it does not evaluate) and two reduced polynomials f₁, f₂ with real coefficients, weighted homogeneous for positive rational weights, each with an isolated critical point at the origin, with ord₀f₁ = 2, ord₀f₂ = 3, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂᴺ, V(f₁), 0) ≅ (ℂᴺ, V(f₂), 0). The construction builds sums of chain singularities from an integer relation among rational weights, matches the spectra modulo 2, obtains an integral Seifert-form isometry (Steenbrink/Némethi and Hertling–Mase/Orlik–Randell for the separate real and integral identifications, then a single integral isometry by strong approximation), applies Levine's classification of simple spherical knots, and extends the link equivalence to an ambient homeomorphism by a weighted cone map. Corollaries in the same manuscript (outside this problem's scope): f₁ and f₂ are topologically right equivalent, Arnold's Hessian-corank question is answered negatively, and initial-form Milnor fibres differ after adding t². (2) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five' (dated 27 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there are reduced convergent holomorphic germs f₄, f₅ : (ℂ⁴, 0) → (ℂ, 0), each with an isolated critical point at 0, with ord₀f₄ = 4, ord₀f₅ = 5, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂ⁴, V(f₄), 0) ≅ (ℂ⁴, V(f₅), 0). The construction starts from the plane curve h = T(X − T²)(X − 2T²) and two degree-four finite graph maps π₀, π₁, whose pullbacks are plane curves of the same embedded type with isometric integral Seifert forms. It smooths the cone yz = w⁴ and adds w(y^a + z^b) to h, with a and b given by formulas in an integer n₀ fixed by congruences. The integral Seifert congruence is obtained by strong approximation, the link equivalence by Kato's Theorem B on Milnor open books of S⁷, and the ambient homeomorphism by an analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4).
events.delivers: For the pair form (two varieties at singular points that are topologically equivalent have equal multiplicity), both manuscripts claim a counterexample for complex hypersurface germs with isolated critical points: multiplicities 2 and 3 in ℂᴺ for some N > 3 divisible by eight (so N ≥ 8), and multiplicities 4 and 5 in ℂ⁴. An ambient homeomorphism of pairs carries V(f) onto V(g), so these pairs are topologically equivalent in the list's sense; the counterexample therefore reaches the list's pair form for reduced hypersurface germs. Both manuscripts describe the result as a negative answer to Zariski's embedded question (paper 1 calls it the 'embedded Zariski multiplicity conjecture'). The statement they prove is the classical hypersurface form, not the list's unrestricted 'varieties'. The family form (b) is not addressed: neither manuscript constructs a topologically equisingular family, and paper 1 says its pair cannot be joined by a μ-constant family and that arbitrary equivalent pairs do not reduce to the family problem.
events.remains: (b) the family form, i.e. whether a topologically equisingular family of singular points has constant multiplicity, is not addressed by either manuscript. (c) Dimension three (ℂ³) is stated by both to remain untreated. Paper 1 does not cover N = 5, 6, 7 or N ≡ 0 mod 8 other than its unspecified N. Paper 2 is specific to N = 4. Plane curves (n = 2) are classically positive per paper 2's introduction (Zariski 1932), so the examples do not reach them. Non-hypersurface varieties, non-isolated singularities, and real or algebraic (non-holomorphic) varieties are not treated. Paper 1 says its construction is not intended to minimize the dimension.
events.doubts: Paper 1: (i) the dimension N is not computed, so the claim is existential; the text says N 'is not intended to minimize' the dimension. (ii) The seed relation rests on finite calculations (a 1118-column cutoff matrix, rank over F₁₀₀₉, an adjugate of an 868-column minor), and the text says a supplied Python program checks them. The repository README says these checks 'cover the finite arithmetic, not the lattice-theoretic or topological arguments'. I did not open or run the programs. (iii) The abstract's topological right equivalence is a corollary, not part of Theorem 1.1, and the source homeomorphism is 'not claimed to be holomorphic or bi-Lipschitz' and need not coincide with the ambient map. (iv) Several results are cited to literature versions, e.g. 'arXiv v3' for Budur et al. Paper 2: (i) the authors flag a limit on a step: 'we do not assert that h is submersive through every value in the disk at θ = 0'; sublevel totals are then isotoped as manifolds with corners. (ii) Thresholds are stated as 'sufficiently large' a, b and 'sufficiently small' s, without numerical bounds; the existence of admissible parameters is a congruence construction. (iii) No computer verification accompanies this paper, and its folder has no verification directory. (iv) Kato's Theorem B is applied to bindings that need not be homotopy spheres; the text cites it rather than re-proving it. (v) I read the statements and the flagged passages of its nine sections, not every proof.; conditional on: No unproven hypothesis is assumed in either theorem; both rest on classical results invoked after their hypotheses are checked. Paper 1 relies on: Levine's classification of simple spherical knots; Thom–Sebastiani and Sakamoto's integral Seifert formula; Steenbrink, Némethi, Hertling–Mase and Orlik–Randell for the real and integral monodromy identifications; Eichler–Kneser–Platonov strong approximation (Rapinchuk, Theorem 2.3); King and Saeki for the right-equivalence corollary, with Sampaio's source-homeomorphism formulation; and Budur et al. (arXiv v3) for the initial-form corollary. Its finite seed relation is established by a computation, not a proof by hand. Paper 2 relies on: Milnor; Némethi's analytic form of Milnor's theorem; Kato's Theorem B (the text notes it needs no homotopy-sphere hypothesis on the binding, citing Kato p.454 and Durfee); Saeki; the analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4); and strong approximation (Platonov, Rapinchuk). Neither paper depends on the other for its proof; paper 2 says the two arguments are independent. The C³ companion (OpenAIMuConstant2026) is cited in paper 1 only in its family discussion, as far as I read.
events.direction: disproves the pair form for complex hypersurface germs, in ℂ⁴ (multiplicities 4 and 5) and in ℂᴺ for some N ≥ 8 divisible by eight (multiplicities 2 and 3); the family form is untouched
events.object: Paper 1: f₁, f₂ are explicit sums of chain polynomials and pure powers with all coefficients 1. Their weights come from an integer relation whose existence the text proves by a finite rank and adjugate computation, and a supplementary explicit relation with 849 nonzero integer coefficients is referenced (verification/support/explicit-relation.json, which I did not open). N is not computed. Paper 2: f₄, f₅ are not written out. They are given as h(p) + w(y^a + z^b) on the smooth fourfold yz = R_s(p,w), with a and b explicit functions of n₀, and then transferred to ℂ⁴ through analytic charts. disputes.summary: Whether the isolated case is settled. Sampaio (arXiv 2503.17127, 2025) says the Zariski conjecture is 'still an open problem even in the case of germ of complex analytic functions with isolated singularities', and also says 'Zariski's Multiplicity Conjecture for families with isolated singularities was confirmed', citing the family result. Auyeung (arXiv 2308.13925, 2023) calls his result a proof of 'Zariski's multiplicity conjecture for isolated hypersurface singularities', and the 2026 Tsinghua course description treats the isolated equisingular-family case as the proved Bobadilla–Pełka theorem. Reading A: the family form for isolated singularities is settled and the pair form is contested. Reading B: the isolated case in the bullet's general form is still open.

summary: The problem is a general open question (topological equisingularity implies equimultiplicity), and the sources read agree that it is still open in general. The main positive result is the family theorem for isolated hypersurfaces: Fernández de Bobadilla and Pełka (arXiv 2204.07007, v1 14 April 2022, opened; Annals of Mathematics 200(1), 2024, accepted 4 March 2024 per the Annals page) prove that a continuous family of power series with finite, constant Milnor number has constant multiplicity. Its arXiv date precedes the window, and the Annals appearance is in 2024. Auyeung (arXiv 2308.13925, 26 August 2023) gives a second proof under an adjacency hypothesis, and Massey (arXiv 2209.03939, 23 August 2022) extends the consequence to aligned non-isolated hypersurfaces. Inside the window, the new preprints each cover a special class. Silva and Silva Júnior (arXiv 2309.02624) first posted surfaces with non-isolated quasihomogeneous singularities in September 2023; their July 2024 version (opened) covers surfaces only and still calls the general conjecture open; their November 2025 version adds quasihomogeneous hypersurfaces of dimensions 3 and 4 under a new title, with no version comment and no journal publication found. Nogueira da Silva and Silva Júnior (arXiv 2509.01634, September 2025) prove the conjecture for one-parameter topologically trivial families of quasihomogeneous corank-one map germs, and say the general conjecture 'remains open'. Fernandes, Jelonek and Sampaio (arXiv 2509.03447, September 2025) prove the metric (ambient bi-Lipschitz) version for multiplicity two; the v2 abstract (December 2025) no longer mentions Zariski. Sampaio (arXiv 2503.17127, March 2025) gives only a conditional reduction, and says the isolated case is still open. Parusiński and Păunescu (arXiv 2602.15192, February 2026) characterise generic Zariski equisingularity of surface singularities in C³ by constancy of an invariant, without addressing topological equisingularity. Silence: no paper in the window is found to be refereed, and the in-window 2025–2026 preprints have no public engagement found, nor any citation beyond Sampaio's and Budur's teaching. Close calls: (a) whether the isolated family theorem counts as a resolution of the bullet, which depends on whether the bullet's pair form is covered by the family form (Sampaio says not, Auyeung and the 2026 course treat the family form as settling the isolated case); (b) whether the Silva–Silva Júnior and Nogueira da Silva results, which are quasihomogeneous and family-restricted, count as settling a class of the bullet's question or as analogues; (c) whether the metric multiplicity-two result is in scope at all, since it replaces topological by bi-Lipschitz equivalence. AI involvement: none was found. Every source read, including the full text or substantial portions of the 2022 Annals-track paper, the 2023 and 2025 Silva papers, Nogueira da Silva 2025, Sampaio 2025, Fernandes et al. 2025 (v2 HTML) and Parusiński–Păunescu 2026, names no AI system. Computer algebra appears in several (Singular in Auyeung's introduction and in Silva's 2024 and 2025 remarks; Surfer for figures in Nogueira da Silva 2025); those are computer-assisted, not AI, and are not recorded under ai.systems. The Lean formalisation of the Annals statement (AnnalsChallenge, lean-eval annals_symplectic_monodromy) is a statement-only formalisation with sorry; no AI system is credited on the pages read. The AI search found only unrelated AI results: an OpenAI unit-distance disproof (May 2026), a Peking University algebra claim, Gemini screens of Erdős problems, and an AI-assisted zero-mass conjecture counterexample. None concerns this problem. A web aggregator's claim of an AI counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture is unrelated and was not checked. The 2019 Łódź paper's remark that the 80-page dBP manuscript had not been published and needed confirmation predates the Annals acceptance; it is recorded in doubts and is not a current objection.
competing_reading: Reading the record as a partial resolution: the isolated family theorem (Bobadilla–Pełka, 2022, published in Annals in 2024, with Auyeung's independent second proof and a 2026 course presenting it) settles the isolated case of the bullet, so the problem has moved inside the window through its 2024 publication and the 2025–2026 partial results add to it. Against: the arXiv date precedes the window, the publication is a journal-timing event, the family form is not the pair form, Sampaio (2025) states that the isolated pair form is still open, and every in-window source calls the general conjecture open. A second competing reading counts the Silva–Silva Júnior (2025) and Nogueira da Silva (2025) papers as settling classes of the bullet's question. Against that: their hypotheses are narrow (quasihomogeneous, corank one, one-parameter, topologically trivial), the same authors wrote all three versions, the scope changed between versions, and no referee or expert check was found.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The Annals article's main theorem as printed, and whether it treats any pair of topologically equivalent isolated germs without a family. The full text was not read (the Annals PDF mirror returned empty; the arXiv PDF was unreadable). (2) Which pairs Sampaio (arXiv 2503.17127) has in mind when he says the isolated case is open. (3) A published review (zbMATH or MathSciNet) of the Bobadilla–Pełka paper stating its scope. (4) Journal acceptance, or a referee or expert report, for the 2023–2025 Silva and Silva Júnior papers and for Nogueira da Silva (2025). (5) The v5 text of arXiv 2204.07007 (5 March 2024), to see what changed inside the window. (6) The Fernandes–Jelonek–Sampaio v1 full text, to confirm the scope of its original Zariski claim. (7) A decision by the judging pass on whether the family form counts for the bullet's pair-and-family statement.

event.what_happened: Two OpenAI manuscripts, each claiming a negative answer to Zariski's question whether embedded topology determines multiplicity for complex hypersurface germs. (1) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurfaces of multiplicities two and three' (dated 24 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there is a finite N > 3 divisible by eight (the text gives N = 4s₀ + 16, where s₀ is the variable count of two seed polynomials fixed by an integer relation it does not evaluate) and two reduced polynomials f₁, f₂ with real coefficients, weighted homogeneous for positive rational weights, each with an isolated critical point at the origin, with ord₀f₁ = 2, ord₀f₂ = 3, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂᴺ, V(f₁), 0) ≅ (ℂᴺ, V(f₂), 0). The construction builds sums of chain singularities from an integer relation among rational weights, matches the spectra modulo 2, obtains an integral Seifert-form isometry (Steenbrink/Némethi and Hertling–Mase/Orlik–Randell for the separate real and integral identifications, then a single integral isometry by strong approximation), applies Levine's classification of simple spherical knots, and extends the link equivalence to an ambient homeomorphism by a weighted cone map. Corollaries in the same manuscript (outside this problem's scope): f₁ and f₂ are topologically right equivalent, Arnold's Hessian-corank question is answered negatively, and initial-form Milnor fibres differ after adding t². (2) 'Ambiently homeomorphic isolated hypersurface germs in ℂ⁴ with multiplicities four and five' (dated 27 September 2026), Theorem 1.1: there are reduced convergent holomorphic germs f₄, f₅ : (ℂ⁴, 0) → (ℂ, 0), each with an isolated critical point at 0, with ord₀f₄ = 4, ord₀f₅ = 5, and a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs (ℂ⁴, V(f₄), 0) ≅ (ℂ⁴, V(f₅), 0). The construction starts from the plane curve h = T(X − T²)(X − 2T²) and two degree-four finite graph maps π₀, π₁, whose pullbacks are plane curves of the same embedded type with isometric integral Seifert forms. It smooths the cone yz = w⁴ and adds w(y^a + z^b) to h, with a and b given by formulas in an integer n₀ fixed by congruences. The integral Seifert congruence is obtained by strong approximation, the link equivalence by Kato's Theorem B on Milnor open books of S⁷, and the ambient homeomorphism by an analytic ambient-pair cone theorem (Massey, Theorem 1.4).
event.delivers: For the pair form (two varieties at singular points that are topologically equivalent have equal multiplicity), both manuscripts claim a counterexample for complex hypersurface germs with isolated critical points: multiplicities 2 and 3 in ℂᴺ for some N > 3 divisible by eight (so N ≥ 8), and multiplicities 4 and 5 in ℂ⁴. The statement they prove is the classical hypersurface form, not the list's unrestricted 'varieties'. The family form (b) is not addressed: neither manuscript constructs a topologically equisingular family, and paper 1 says its pair cannot be joined by a μ-constant family and that arbitrary equivalent pairs do not reduce to the family problem.

judgement.why: The Zariski multiplicity conjecture is a universal implication (topological equivalence/equisingularity implies equal multiplicity). The OpenAI manuscripts claim pairs of isolated complex hypersurface germs, ambiently homeomorphic, with multiplicities 4 vs 5 in C^4 and 2 vs 3 in C^N; if correct, a single such pair refutes the conjecture as stated (classically, and in the list's wording, the pair question), so I score it whole/refuted/counterexample, unreviewed, doubtful rather than credible given its age and the unverified existential steps; the README quote credits the model with producing the results, so generated. The family form being untouched does not save the conjecture, since the counterexample contradicts the statement's assertion directly. All other post-snapshot events are special classes (case), metric analogues (variant), or reductions/neighbouring results (none). Bobadilla–Pełka is dated to its April 2022 arXiv v1 (v5 in March 2024 not shown to contain new mathematics) and is a digested case, not whole, since it covers only μ-constant isolated families.
judgement.doubts: Close call on whole vs case for openai-math-059: the bullet loosely names both equisingularity (family form) and equimultiplicity; I read a counterexample to the pair form as refuting the conjecture outright, but a reader taking the family form as the conjecture would score it case. The record also notes the 'universal' readings of 'varieties' exceed hypersurfaces, which a counterexample covers anyway. Pre-snapshot verification calls for journal items rest on citations, not opened papers; they do not affect the outcome. Whether the C^N construction actually yields a germ of the claimed form depends on an unrun computation.
